h1:
Saraburi–Lopburi 2 Days 1 Night
Ancient City, Monkeys & Sunflower Fields
intro: Saraburi and Lopburi sit right next to each other — barely an hour's drive apart — so combining them into one cross-province trip is a no-brainer. Day one covers Saraburi's temples and nature spots, you stay overnight, then day two crosses into Lopburi for the old Lavo city ruins, the infamous resident monkeys, and (in winter) the sunflower fields along Pa Sak Dam. This is a route timed so you never feel rushed and actually get to see both towns properly.

blocks.html: What makes this trip work is that you cover three completely different vibes without driving far — mountain waterfalls and temple grounds in Saraburi, then centuries-old Khmer ruins and colonial-era mansions in Lopburi, and finally a valley full of yellow sunflowers closing things out. It's a solid two-day escape for Bangkok locals who don't want to burn vacation days, or anyone who enjoys driving a scenic route.

One honest heads-up before you plan: Lopburi's sunflower fields only bloom in winter, roughly late November through mid-January. Outside that window, the plots are bare farmland or planted with other crops. The Saraburi day-one sights and Lopburi's historical old city are worth visiting year-round, so coming outside sunflower season is still a good trip — just don't plan around the flowers.

items: Distances — Bangkok to Saraburi city: ~110 km (about 1.5 hrs) · Saraburi to Lopburi city centre: ~45 km (45 min–1 hr)
Own car recommended — This is the easiest way to do this trip. Attractions are spread out, and the sunflower fields in particular are hard to reach by public transport.
No car? — Take the Northern Line train to Lopburi station. The old city sights are all walkable from there. For the sunflower fields you'll need to hire a local taxi or songthaew for a half-day.
Accommodation — Overnight in Lopburi city or near Mueang Kaew (close to Pa Sak Dam), depending on where you finish day one.

blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Saraburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 1 — Saraburi: Temple, Waterfall, Dairy Farm

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Saraburi Side — Phra Phutthabat, Waterfalls & the Dairy Farm

items.note: Leaving early avoids mid-morning traffic and gives you a full day. Grab breakfast once you reach Saraburi town.
One of Thailand's most revered temples, housing a gilded pavilion over the Buddha's Footprint. Open roughly 08:00–17:00. Free for Thai nationals. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees covered.
A tiered limestone waterfall in Muak Lek district, good for wading at midday to cool off. During the rainy season water levels run high and the rocks get slippery — watch your footing.
The area has several steak restaurants and riverside eateries. It's a small, pleasant town with good air.
Feed the cows, taste fresh milk and real dairy ice cream. Kids love it. Tractor rides around the farm cost extra.
Stay in Muak Lek if you prefer a mountain feel, or push ahead to Lopburi city to get an early start on day two.

blocks.title: Pick your overnight spot based on day-two plans
blocks.html: If you want to catch the sunflower fields at sunrise on day two, stay near Lopburi or close to Pa Sak Dam. That way you can be there by 8 a.m. without a 4 a.m. alarm.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Lopburi: Old City & Sunflower Fields

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Lopburi Side — Lavo Ruins, Monkeys & Yellow Fields

items.activity: Khao Chin Lae Sunflower Fields / Pa Sak Jolasid Dam
items.note: Winter only (late Nov–mid Jan). Aim to arrive 8–10 a.m. for good light and smaller crowds. Entry per plot: around THB 20–30. Some spots have bicycles to rent.
Three-pronged Khmer prang right in the town centre — Lopburi's most iconic landmark. Entry for Thai nationals: THB 10. Note: this is a major monkey zone. Keep bags closed and hold your glasses.
Ruins of a European-style mansion from King Narai's era, built to host foreign envoys. Good for photos among old brick walls and archways.
The historic district has several long-running noodle shops, rice-curry spots, and dessert stalls all within walking distance.
King Narai's royal palace, now a museum. Open Wed–Sun 08:30–16:30. Entry for Thai nationals: THB 30. Closed Monday–Tuesday — factor this into your planning.
A cluster of ancient prangs and chedis directly across from the train station. Good for a slow walk through Lavo–Ayutthaya-era architecture before heading home.

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs and head back
items.note: Lopburi's popular souvenirs are dried mee noodles and Chinese pastries (khnom pia). Bangkok is about 2–2.5 hrs from here.

blocks.title: What you need to know about the monkeys before you go
blocks.html: The macaques around Phra Prang Sam Yot and Lopburi train station are fast and clever. Don't carry visible food bags or water bottles, tuck away glasses, hats, and phones, and close your car windows if you park anywhere in the old city.

blocks.text: When the Sunflower Fields Actually Bloom

blocks.html: This is the part many visitors get wrong. The Lopburi sunflower fields are not a year-round attraction — they follow a winter planting cycle, generally blooming from late November through mid-January. Individual plots don't all peak at the same time; some may be fading while others are just opening up. Before you go, check the farm's social pages or ask locally which plots are currently at their best.

items: Khao Chin Lae / Nikhom Sang Ton-eng zone — Large fields covering hundreds of rai with mountain backdrops; the go-to photo spot.
Roadside plots along Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, Phatthana Nikhom district — Fields scattered in patches along the road; nice to drive through as a route. Dam open 06:30–18:00.
Best time of day — 8–10 a.m. The flowers face the morning light and temperatures are still comfortable. By late morning it's bright, hot, and busier.
Entry fees — Most plots charge around THB 20–30 per person. Some offer bicycle or tram rentals inside the fields.

blocks.text: Adjusting the Plan for Your Group

items.name: Travelling with kids
items.blurb: Prioritise the dairy farm and Chet Sao Noi waterfall on day one. On day two, pick a sunflower plot with bikes to rent — kids enjoy pedalling through the fields far more than touring old temples all day.

items.name: History buffs
items.blurb: Give Lopburi a full day. Take your time at all four sites: Phra Prang Sam Yot, Vichayen House, Narai Ratchaniwet Palace, and Wat Phra Si Ratana Mahathat. None of them rush well.

items.name: No car — train option
items.blurb: Take the Northern Line to Lopburi station and walk the entire old city circuit — everything is close. For the sunflower fields, hire a local taxi or tuk-tuk for a half-day return trip.

items: Entrance fees for the whole trip — Temples, old-city sites, and sunflower plots combined: roughly THB 100–200 per person (Thai nationals).
One night's accommodation — Guesthouses and small hotels start around THB 600–900; mid-range around THB 1,200–2,000/night.
Food — Around THB 60–150 per person per meal. Eating in both towns is genuinely affordable.
Petrol / transport — Bangkok round trip by car: roughly THB 700–1,000 per vehicle, depending on route and number of stops.

faq.q: How many days do you need for a Saraburi–Lopburi trip?
faq.a: Two days, one night is the sweet spot. Day one covers Saraburi (Phra Phutthabat, waterfall, dairy farm), you stay overnight, then day two is Lopburi's old city and the sunflower fields. You can technically squeeze it into one day, but it'll feel rushed and tiring.

faq.q: When do the Lopburi sunflower fields bloom?
faq.a: Winter only — roughly late November through mid-January. Individual plots peak at different times, so check local social pages before you go. Arriving around 8–10 a.m. gives you the best light and fewer crowds. Outside the bloom season the fields are empty farmland.

faq.q: Do I really need to watch out for monkeys in Lopburi?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely. The macaques around Phra Prang Sam Yot and Lopburi train station are bold and fast. Don't carry visible food or open water bottles, keep glasses, hats, and phones tucked away, and close car windows when parked in the old city area.

faq.q: Can I do this trip without a car?
faq.a: Partly. Take the Northern Line train to Lopburi station and you can walk the entire old-city circuit easily — the sights are all right there. But the sunflower fields and Saraburi attractions are outside town and difficult to reach by public transport. You'd need to hire a local taxi or songthaew for those.

faq.q: Is Narai Ratchaniwet Palace open every day?
faq.a: No — it's closed Monday and Tuesday. Open Wednesday through Sunday, 08:30–16:30. Entry for Thai nationals is THB 30. If the palace museum is on your list, make sure day two of your trip falls on a Wednesday to Sunday.
